+Caching of related model instances
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+When traversing relations, the ORM will avoid re-fetching objects that were
+previously loaded. For example, with the tutorial's models::
+

+    >>> first_choice = first_poll.choice_set.all()[0]
+    >>> first_choice.poll is first_poll
+    True

+
+For one-to-one relationships, both sides can be cached. For many-to-one

I have resolved the issue in [related_descriptors.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-30y6xe14/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py).

### Cause
When prefetching related objects via [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-30y6xe14/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-30y6xe14/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L366-L383), and [`create_reverse_many_to_one_manager.<locals>.RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-30y6xe14/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L635-L655), Django pre-populates the reverse relation cache on each prefetched object with the parent `instance`. When the parent `instance` has deferred fields (e.g., from `.only()` or `.defer()`), setting it in the reverse cache causes subsequent nested `Prefetch` lookups back to the parent model to treat the relation as already fetched (`is_fetched(obj) == True`), discarding the newly queried parent instances (which had the expected deferred/loaded fields) and leaving the original deferred parent instance in the cache.

### Solution
Only populate the reverse relation cache in `get_prefetch_queryset()` when the parent `instance` has no deferred fields (`not instance.get_deferred_fields()`).
